title: Static finite Gibbs data do not identify a canonical heat-root incidence
question: Does a fixed finite energy and Gibbs density determine the mobility, heat rates, or root-incidence order required by the A13 production owner?
purpose: Construct two exact positive mobility generators with the same finite quadratic Gibbs density and different coordinate heat rates. This isolates the missing dynamic owner without pretending that a generic witness is the full A1 production functional.

registered_inputs.generator: L_M f = -<M grad F,grad f> + beta^-1 tr(M Hess f)

derived_contract.necessary_missing_owner: mobility/heat-root incidence plus raw-current spatial intertwiner

hostile_mutations: replace mobility B by mobility A
claim same heat rates from same Gibbs density
identify the witness energy with the complete A1 F_ref
swap root labels without recomputing the coordinate assignment
claim a heat-root map from static covariance alone
insert a Lean sorry or axiom token
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite mobility non-identifiability witness only. The two generators share the witness Gibbs density and static Hessian but have different heat rates and root-labelled decay. This does not identify or refute the canonical A1 production generator, heat-root incidence, raw-current spatial intertwiner, conditional replicas, q-ledger, A13/T-050, Sector-A, Pre-A, physical-empty, continuum, thermodynamic, or real-time conclusions.
next_action: Supply a hash-pinned production mobility/heat-root map and raw-current spatial intertwiner on the same A1 cylinder; only then rerun the R192 owner-slot audit and any q-ledger estimate.
